response: Late-night salivary cortisol is not a better screening test for possible cortisol excess than standard screening tests in obese patients with Type 2 diabetes. In fact, it has a poor specificity for cortisol excess in this population. A 24-hour urinary free cortisol (UFC) test shows significantly better specificity in screening for cortisol excess in obese patients with Type 2 diabetes. Therefore, standard screening tests, such as the 24-hour UFC test, are more effective in identifying cortisol excess in this group of patients.
